title: Preserve v1 data and establish migration regression fixtures
scope: Extract the actual 37 task IDs and inventory every existing interaction. Create synthetic v1 backups spanning completions, all scores, journal and achievements; no real learner data.
accept: All 37 IDs including w1–w12 retain meaning; six score categories remain intact.
Tests prove v1 import preserves values and malformed/unsupported imports leave current state untouched.
Record baseline browser flows and recovery steps before modularization.

title: Modularize the app with TypeScript and deploy a Pages build
scope: Introduce Vite and lightweight modules while preserving app behavior. Configure CI build and GitHub Pages repository subpath; document rollback.
accept: Existing roadmap, filters, ratings, journal, achievements, export/import and reset still work.
Build and browser smoke tests cover /ciso-journey/, refresh and asset URLs.
Document run/test/deploy commands and deployed-origin backup migration.

title: Implement versioned transactional storage and complete backups
scope: Define storage boundaries, evaluate IndexedDB, and implement recoverable migrations plus a schema-versioned backup envelope extensible to learning history.
accept: Migrations are transactional/idempotent; original v1 state remains recoverable until success.
Full export/import round-trips all introduced entities and rejects corrupt/future input without writes.
Storage failure/quota cases give actionable recovery rather than silently resetting progress.

title: Design curriculum coverage and measurable learning objectives
scope: Map ten domains, all 37 actual tasks and six existing competencies to versioned NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CISSP and CISM outcomes; prioritize weeks 1–4.
accept: Coverage matrix includes secure software, cloud, cryptography, networking and leadership.
Each foundation objective is observable and has prerequisites plus a planned assessment.
CISSP outline validity dates and Swiss/EU scope are explicit; record unresolved learner preferences in memory.

title: Define content schemas and an editorial publication gate
scope: Model lessons, concepts, questions, cards, sources, scenarios, rubrics and versioned mappings. Build validators and an authoring/review checklist.
accept: Stable IDs, relationships, content versions and source/review metadata validate automatically.
Draft, source-checked, independently reviewed, published, stale and retired states are distinct.
No AI-only draft is labeled independently reviewed; legal claims require verified authoritative text.
Content corrections preserve prior attempt versions; copyright constraints and review cadence documented.

title: Build the original lesson reader and concept navigation
scope: Provide structured reading with objectives, sections, examples, references, prerequisites and concept links; record reading progress independently.
accept: A learner can study a complete unit without paid external material.
Keyboard/mobile reader and safe rendering of authored/imported content are checked.
Reading completion does not mark a task or competency mastered.

title: Author and review original lessons for foundation weeks 1–4
scope: Produce at least four substantive original lessons aligned to actual w1–w4 tasks, with executive examples, misconceptions, practice and supplementary LinkedIn links.
accept: Every objective has adequate explanatory reading and a worked example, not only a definition/link list.
At least 12 curated cards, 20 questions spanning all three formats, and one case reference stable concepts/sources.
Reviewer status is truthful; unresolved factual/source concerns prevent validated publication.

title: Track learning resources independently and preserve custom resources
scope: Implement README resource progress stories with stable resource IDs, dates, notes and custom links. Courses supplement original teaching.
accept: Course completion changes resource state only; task/recall/mastery stay unchanged.
Discovery searches are labeled; resource edits/archival preserve historical progress.
Custom-resource lifecycle, safe URL handling and backup round-trip are verified.

title: Implement question banks and explained assessment attempts
scope: Support MCQ, scenario-based and open-ended questions with objective links, versioned attempts, feedback and retry behavior.
accept: Every MCQ option has an explanation; feedback appears after an attempted answer.
Scenario/open-ended responses use explicit rubrics and annotated examples, not string matching.
Attempts retain content version and assessment provenance; quiz score does not confer applied mastery.

title: Implement deterministic FSRS review scheduling and durable history
scope: Integrate a pinned ts-fsrs version behind an adapter, four ratings, complete scheduler state, append-only events, due queues and configurable new-card caps.
accept: Clock-controlled tests cover all ratings, overdue cards, timezone boundaries and refresh/backup restoration.
Event and scheduler writes are atomic; double submits do not schedule twice.
Store library/scheduler/content versions and preserve history for edited, suspended or archived cards.
Again means failed recall; Hard means successful effortful recall; no ratings mutate competency.

title: Build prompt-first daily review and the foundation Today flow
scope: Connect original reading, questions, due reviews and one related exercise in a manageable daily study loop.
accept: Answer is hidden until reveal; keyboard-accessible Again/Hard/Good/Easy follow reveal.
Due reviews have priority, new-card limits are configurable and overdue work survives missed days.
Show distinct reading/resource/task/recall/assessment signals and an honest time estimate.
End-to-end foundation flow works on mobile and survives restart/export/import.

title: Deliver the first executive simulation with rubric and evidence
scope: Provide one executive decision case with impact, options, accountable owner, recommendation, residual risk and evidence metadata.
accept: A complete worked response and Recognize/Explain/Apply/Lead rubric explain tradeoffs.
Self-assessed vs independently reviewed evidence is explicit; old 0–4 ratings remain separate.
Evidence links/notes stay private and round-trip; no binary/public upload assumed.

title: Verify and release the complete weeks 1–4 learning loop
scope: Run release-gate verification across original lessons, questions, retrieval, practice, data preservation and Pages deployment.
accept: All R0 and R1 gates in PLAN.md pass with recorded test/content-review evidence.
Invalid imported markup/URLs cannot execute; essential keyboard/mobile flows pass.
Release notes disclose provisional content and retain recovery/export instructions.

title: Complete original foundation teaching for weeks 5–12
scope: Write at least eight further substantial lessons with cards, questions, worked examples and exercises mapped to w5–w12.
accept: All 12 weekly tasks have original teaching and assessments for their stated outcomes.
Content passes schema/source/pedagogy review; cards are curated instead of mechanically generated.
Previously studied content versions and progress survive expansion.

title: Add six competency cases, practical portfolio and quarterly reassessment
scope: Expand to one executive case per legacy competency and practical artifacts such as risk register, ISMS gap analysis, incident tabletop and board report.
accept: Six cases have decision tradeoffs, rubrics and annotated responses.
Quarterly assessments record level, provenance, evidence and date without overwriting original scores.
Portfolio metadata, private notes and assessment history survive backups.

title: Show retention, assessment and evidence trends honestly
scope: Build progress views separating observed retrieval performance, FSRS estimates, rubric assessments, milestones and portfolio evidence.
accept: No single readiness/mastery percent or certificate eligibility claim.
Time windows, sample sizes and estimated-vs-observed measures are visible.
Trends derive from durable versioned events and handle no-data cases.

title: Publish advanced curriculum across architecture, risk and operations
scope: Deliver original advanced teaching for architecture/IAM, asset protection, secure delivery/cloud, risk, operations, incidents, resilience and third parties.
accept: Every relevant task/objective in the coverage matrix has reviewed lessons, questions, cards and practical cases.
Source mappings are versioned; revised frameworks do not silently rewrite prior attempts.
Editorial gaps remain visible rather than presenting placeholder lessons as complete.

title: Publish Swiss/EU compliance, governance and executive leadership teaching
scope: Deliver original ISMS/audit, privacy/regulatory, strategy/budget, board communication, culture/ethics and AI governance units.
accept: Verify current FADP, GDPR, NIS2, DORA and relevant Swiss sector guidance against official texts before claims are published.
Explain jurisdiction, entity/sector applicability, effective dates and national implementation; do not imply every rule applies to every Swiss learner.
Original board/budget/leadership cases and ISO/NIST/CISSP/CISM mappings complete all 37 tasks across ten domains.
Independent review status and stale-content handling are explicit.

title: Create explainable personalized learning paths
scope: Use prerequisite gaps, due reviews, assessed weaknesses, learner goals and time budget to recommend next study; start with deterministic rules.
accept: Explain why each recommendation appears and allow learner override.
Tests cover cold start, conflicting goals, prerequisite cycles, scarce time and overdue load.
No recommendation infers applied competency from course/flashcard success; preference changes persist.

title: Design private sync, threat model and conflict semantics
scope: Evaluate sync provider, auth, region, recovery and threat model; specify append-only reviews, note conflicts, deletes/tombstones and transactional boundaries.
accept: Record provider/region and identity decisions in MEMORY.md before infrastructure work.
Define account switching, sign-out/local data, duplicate/out-of-order events, same-card concurrent reviews and deletion semantics.
Define export/deletion/recovery and evidence privacy; browser secrets/service-role keys forbidden.

title: Implement optional authenticated cross-device synchronization
scope: Add private user-owned sync with enforced server authorization, durable offline queues and explicit conflict UI.
accept: Two devices converge through reconnect/retry without duplicate review events or silent conflicting-note loss.
Two-account tests prove isolation, including malicious ownership updates and storage policies if used.
Sign-out/account switching cannot expose another account; server deletions are not resurrected offline.
Local-only mode and complete backups remain available; no privileged frontend credentials.
